**Arduino Based Ultrasonic Distance Measurement**

*Aim*

To interface an HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor with an Arduino UNO 

*Introduction*

1. The ultrasonic sensor is an electronic device used to measure the distance of an object without physical contact. It works by transmitting ultrasonic sound waves and receiving the reflected waves from an object.  
     
2. In this project, an HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor is connected to an Arduino UNO. The Arduino sends a trigger signal to the sensor 

 *Components Required*

*  Arduino UNO  
*  HC-SR04 Ultrasonic Sensor  
*  Breadboard  
*  Jumper Wires  
*  USB Cable  
*  Computer/Laptop

*Circuit Connections*

* HC-SR04 Pin| Arduino UNO  
* VCC| 5V  
* GND| GND  
* TRIG| Digital Pin 9  
* ECHO| Digital Pin 10

![circuit](circuit..jpg)

*SCHEMATIC DIAGRAM*  
*![simulation](simulation..jpg)

 *Working Principle*

1. The HC-SR04 works based on the time-of-flight principle.

2. First, the Arduino sends a short HIGH pulse to the TRIG pin of the ultrasonic sensor. The sensor then sends ultrasonic waves towards the object.  
     
3. When the ultrasonic waves hit an object, they are reflected back towards the sensor. The ECHO pin receives the reflected signal. Arduino measures the time taken for the ultrasonic wave to travel to the object and return.

*Arduino Program*

int trig \= 9;  
int echo \= 10;

void setup() {  
  Serial.begin(9600);  
  pinMode(trig, OUTPUT);  
  pinMode(echo, INPUT);  
}

void loop() {

  digitalWrite(trig, HIGH);  
  delayMicroseconds(10);  
  digitalWrite(trig, LOW);

  long result \= pulseIn(echo, HIGH);

  Serial.println(result);

  delay(1000);  
}

*Procedure*

*  Connect the HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor to the breadboard.  
*  Connect the VCC of the sensor to the 5V pin of the Arduino.  
*  Connect the GND of the sensor to the Arduino GND.  
*  Connect TRIG to digital pin 9\.  
*  Connect ECHO to digital pin 10\.  
*  Connect the Arduino UNO to the computer using a USB cable.  
*  Upload the Arduino program.  
*  Open the Serial Monitor.  
*  Place an object in front of the ultrasonic sensor.  
*  Observe the distance value displayed in centimetres.

 *Applications*

The ultrasonic sensor can be used in:

* Obstacle detection systems  
* Automatic parking systems  
*  Smart dustbins  
*  Robotics  
* Automatic door systems  
* Water-level monitoring  
* Railway crossing safety systems  
*  Object detection systems  
* Distance measurement projects  
*  Smart automation systems

*Advantages*

*  Non-contact distance measurement  
*  Easy to interface with Arduino  
*  Low cost  
*  Simple circuit connection  
*  Useful for real-time applications  
*  Suitable for beginner-level Arduino projects

 *Result*

The HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor was successfully interfaced with the Arduino UNO. The distance between the sensor and the object was measured and displayed in centimetres on the Serial Monitor.  
![result](Result.jpg)

 *Conclusion*

This project demonstrates the use of an ultrasonic sensor with an Arduino for distance measurement. The sensor detects an object by transmitting and receiving ultrasonic waves, while the Arduino calculates the distance based on the time taken by the waves to return. This basic concept can be further developed into various real-time automation and safety applications.
